se: The meeting noted the summary of its work in fiscal year 2025, such as gathering information on petitions, studying the draft labour protection law on maternity leave, and studying the ratification of ILO Conventions No. 87 and No. 98
it: Summary of work, fiscal year 2025

te: Labour problems in the film and entertainment industry heard
se: The meeting heard people working in the film industry and the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare, who described problems such as inadequate pay, no overtime pay and safety risks, and noted that many workers do not yet know their rights
it: Labour problems in the film and entertainment industry

te: Independent workers heard on the draft law on independent workers
se: The meeting heard groups of independent workers and civil society, who object to defining platform workers as "semi-independent workers" in the draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. .... and want their status recognised as "employees" under the Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998)
it: Draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. ....

te: Study topics set on platform work, AI and migrant workers
se: The meeting set its study topics, such as platform employment, which has no specific law yet, the effects of artificial intelligence on employment, Thai soft power and an ageing society, improving labour relations law, and welfare protection for migrant workers
it: The subcommittee's study topics

te: Draft report on ILO Conventions No. 87 and No. 98 revised
se: The meeting considered the draft report on ratifying International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions No. 87 and No. 98, resolving that some wording be revised and that information from the lecture by the ILO Subregional Office for East Asia be added to complete it
it: Draft report on ratifying International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions No. 87 and No. 98

te: Principles of the draft digital platform economy law heard
se: The meeting heard the Electronic Transactions Development Agency and the Office of the Council of State on the objectives of the draft Digital Platform Economy Act B.E. ...., which aims to protect consumers, create fair competition and prevent wrongdoing through platforms
it: Draft Digital Platform Economy Act B.E. ....

te: Ministry of Labour heard on the principles of the draft law on independent workers
se: The meeting noted the principles and reasons of the draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. .... from representatives of the Ministry of Labour and academics, who explained that this kind of work is neither a traditional contract of employment nor a contract for work, but a special kind of contract
it: Draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. ....

te: Riders heard on the draft law on independent workers
se: The meeting heard representatives of riders' groups, who disagree with the draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. .... because they want the law to name riders clearly rather than group them as independent or semi-independent workers
it: Draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. ....

te: Calls heard to speed up the laws on independent workers and digital platforms
se: The meeting noted a petition asking the legislature to help push the draft Independent Workers Promotion and Protection Act B.E. .... and the draft Digital Platform Economy Act B.E. .... into force, and scheduled further hearings for the next meeting
it: Petition asking for the laws on independent workers and digital platforms to be pushed forward

te: Study visits on workplace safety prepared, and a framework for the ILO report set
se: The meeting prepared study visits on occupational safety, health and the working environment in Chon Buri Province on 28 April 2025 and in Songkhla and Satun Provinces on 7–10 May 2025, and set the framework for the report on ratifying International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions No. 87 and No. 98
it: Study visits to Chon Buri, Songkhla and Satun Provinces
Framework for the report on ratifying International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions No. 87 and No. 98

se: The meeting approved the report on its consideration of a petition about a dispute between a former employee and an employer, for submission to the Committee on Labour, and considered the summary report on approaches to protecting and assisting employees to ease the problem of unfair dismissal
it: Report on the petition about a dispute between a former employee and an employer
Summary report on approaches to protecting and assisting employees to ease the problem of unfair dismissal

te: End proposed to a former employee's petition, and a dismissal case followed up
se: The meeting agreed to inform the committee that consideration of the petition about a dispute between a former employee and an employer should end, as the petitioner could not be contacted and it is a private dispute over conditions of employment. It continued to consider a petition concerning the dismissal of employees of an automotive parts manufacturer
it: Petition on a dispute between a former employee and an employer
Petition concerning the dismissal of employees of an automotive parts manufacturer

te: Dismissal case followed up, and study of ILO Conventions No. 87 and No. 98 begins
se: The meeting heard the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare on the use of labour inspectors' powers under section 139 of the Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) in dismissal cases, and heard the key points of ILO Conventions No. 87 and No. 98, to study the ratification of International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions No. 87 and No. 98
it: Progress on a petition concerning the dismissal of employees of an automotive parts manufacturer
Ratification of International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions No. 87 and No. 98

te: Further information on a dismissal case received, and an approach to an ILO visit set
se: The meeting noted further information from the Legal Execution Department and the police officers concerned for preparing approaches to protecting and assisting employees to ease the problem of unfair dismissal, resolved to invite the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare to give information at the next meeting, and considered its approach to a study visit to the International Labour Organization office
it: Approaches to protecting and assisting employees to ease the problem of unfair dismissal
Approach to the study visit to the International Labour Organization office

te: Draft approaches to easing the problem of unfair dismissal
se: The meeting considered the draft approaches to protecting and assisting employees to ease the problem of unfair dismissal, based on the case study above, and agreed to add information on receivership and the progress of the legal case, and to propose stronger measures, such as a fund to help employees in cases of this kind
it: Draft approaches to protecting and assisting employees to ease the problem of unfair dismissal

te: Issues set for following up a case of dismissed employees
se: The meeting set issues for following up a petition concerning the dismissal of employees of an automotive parts manufacturer, such as payments from the Employee Welfare Fund as reported by the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare, the progress of the legal case, and further information on severance payments
it: Petition concerning the dismissal of employees of an automotive parts manufacturer
